title: Regular integral coefficients commute with scheme pullback
statement: For ℓ prime, E a normed field over Q_ℓ, a scheme map f:Y→X, and an endomorphism p of the regular integral coefficient module, conjugate normalized pullback of p by the regular comparison [def-weil-pbc-integral-matrix-analytic-data]. Its canonical continuous coefficient at y is the coefficient of p at f(y). No matrix or cokernel hypothesis is required.

source.place: Section 6.8, Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(1): integral coefficient framework and kernel-closure application; the displayed continuous-function pivot argument is an agent reduction, not a matrix argument written out in Lemma 6.8.7

proof.text: The underlying regular-module pullback is the inverse-image endomorphism conjugated by the coefficient comparison. Naturality of the inverse-image adjunction unit gives commutation with the canonical coefficient pushforward.
Transport the resulting endomorphism square through the scheme-natural continuous coefficient chart.

Evaluate the continuous-sheaf square on the global unit. The pullback of the unit is the unit. Naturality with the final object on Y and evaluation along the canonical pullback section identify the two values at y and f(y).

proof_origin.place: Section 6.8, continuous coefficient framework; analytic matrix-chart reduction
proof_origin.note: The matrix argument is an agent reduction, not a matrix argument stated in Lemma 6.8.7.

lean.statement:
theorem integralRegularCoefficient_pullback (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (E : Type) [NormedField E] [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[ℓ] E]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (p : Mod.regular (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X) ⟶
      Mod.regular (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X)) (y : Y) :
    integralRegularCoefficient ℓ E Y
      ((integralRegularPullbackIso ℓ E f).inv ≫
        (integralMatrixPullback ℓ E f).map p ≫
          (integralRegularPullbackIso ℓ E f).hom) y =
      integralRegularCoefficient ℓ E X p (f y)
